NDT training in Omaha: how it works for Omaha employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training to Omaha employers and technicians, either as live online theory, onsite at your own facility, or a blend of the two, under ASNT Level III oversight. Atlantis has no classroom building in Omaha or anywhere in Nebraska. Your employer's written practice defines certification, a Level III gives the exams, and the employer certifies you. Structural steel fabricators, rail and utility contractors, power plant maintenance teams and inspection companies use the training for UT, PAUT, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET.

Omaha's inspection market looks different from the coastal refinery towns. Much of the work is production weld inspection in fabrication shops, structural and bridge inspection, rail, power generation, and ethanol and agricultural processing plants spread across Nebraska and western Iowa. Many Omaha technicians also travel: national engineering and construction firms headquartered here staff QA/QC roles on projects across the country. Whether you are in a shop on the edge of town or on a project three states away, the questions are the same. Is the procedure qualified? Is the person certified to the employer's written practice for this method and level? Will the records satisfy the owner, the customer or the auditor?

Most Omaha-area enquiries come from four groups. First, steel fabricators producing poles, towers, irrigation structures, bridge girders and building steel, who weld to AWS D1.1 and, for bridges, AWS D1.5. Second, utility and power teams maintaining coal, gas and nuclear plants in eastern Nebraska. Third, rail-related shops and contractors serving the railroads headquartered and operating in the region. Fourth, construction and engineering firms that need field QA/QC technicians certified before they mobilise. Each group needs a different mix of methods, so we build the course plan around your scope. Request an Omaha training quote and tell us what your people inspect.

Omaha, the Nebraska hub and Level III consulting: where each page fits

This page covers training for Omaha employers and technicians. For statewide coverage, including Lincoln, Grand Island and western Nebraska, see NDT training in Nebraska. If you need a Level III to write procedures, review a written practice or act as your outside Level III, see NDT Level III consulting in Omaha, nuclear NDT consulting in Omaha, and NDT consulting across Nebraska. Many clients use both services: consulting to put the written practice in order, then training to qualify the crew against it.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Omaha

Every course follows the ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice. Level I and Level II courses cover principles, equipment, calibration, technique, and interpretation against an approved procedure. Level III preparation covers the Basic examination, method examinations, and the procedure-writing and programme skills a Level III needs. SNT-TC-1A's recommended training hours and experience for each method and level are in our training-requirements matrix. Your written practice can require more.

MethodLevelsWhat Omaha employers use it forPrerequisite
UT (ultrasonic testing)I, II, III prepFull-penetration welds on poles, towers and bridge members, thickness surveys on tanks and piping, rail and axle inspectionBasic algebra; Level I before Level II
PAUT (phased array UT)II, III prepWeld examination on heavy structural and pressure welds, corrosion mapping on ethanol plant tanks and pipingUT Level II or concurrent UT training, per written practice
TOFD (time-of-flight diffraction)IIHeight sizing on thick butt welds in power plant and heavy fabrication workUT Level II
RT (radiographic testing)I, II, III prepPipeline and plant piping weld radiography, castings, film and digital interpretationRadiation safety training plus Nebraska licensing requirements for source handlers
MT (magnetic particle testing)I, II, III prepToe cracks and base-plate welds on poles and towers, structural connections, rail components, castingsNone beyond employer entry rules
PT (liquid penetrant testing)I, II, III prepStainless piping in food, ethanol and pharmaceutical plants, non-magnetic partsNone beyond employer entry rules
VT (visual testing)I, II, III prepProduction weld visual acceptance, bridge and structure condition surveys, field QA/QCNone beyond employer entry rules
ET (eddy current testing)I, II, III prepCondenser and heat-exchanger tubes at power plants, surface cracks on non-ferrous components, aircraft partsBasic electrical theory helps

For a structural fabricator, VT, MT and UT Level II usually come first because they cover most production weld acceptance. Power and process plant teams need UT thickness, PT and ET. Field QA/QC technicians for national construction projects often need VT, MT and UT together. Tell us where your crew works and we will recommend a sequence.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Omaha, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. A training provider, college or state agency does not certify you. Your employer does, under its written practice. The sequence an Omaha technician goes through:

  1. The employer's written practice. Your employer documents how it trains, examines and certifies personnel by method and level. If you need one, see written-practice development.
  2. Formal training hours. Classroom or live-online instruction at the hours the written practice sets. Atlantis delivers this part. Minimums are in the requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised experience in the method on your employer's work, logged and signed.
  4. General, specific and practical examinations. Given by a Level III or designated examiner under the written practice. The practical uses real specimens and real equipment.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, at least annually as the written practice requires.
  6. Certification by the employer. The employer signs, supported by the Level III's records.
  7. Recertification. At the written-practice interval, by evidence of continued satisfactory work or re-examination.

If you change employers, your certification does not transfer automatically. The new employer certifies you under its own written practice, using your training and experience records as evidence. Keep copies. For the full employer model see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Omaha crews

Omaha teams train with Atlantis in one of three ways.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions with a Level III on a timetable that fits shift work and travel. This suits individual technicians, small shops and field staff who are rarely in one place. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. We bring the course to your shop or plant and use your instruments and representative parts as specimens where the written practice allows. Fabricators with several new inspectors usually find this the most efficient option.
  • Blended. Theory online first, then a compact onsite block for hands-on technique and practical examinations under Level III supervision.

Plan around the calendar. Power plant outages in the region usually fall in spring and autumn, construction mobilisations peak in the warmer months, and fabrication shops have their own production peaks. We schedule cohorts so new Level IIs are certified before the busy period, not during it. Ask about onsite training for your Omaha crew. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day. Employers with several plants or branches can look at corporate NDT training programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Omaha

  • Structural steel and fabrication. Omaha is home to manufacturers of utility poles, telecom and lighting structures, irrigation systems and building steel, plus many smaller fabricators. Production welds are inspected to AWS D1.1, and bridge members to AWS D1.5. VT, MT and UT are the core methods.
  • Power generation. Omaha Public Power District and Nebraska Public Power District run coal and gas stations in eastern Nebraska, and Cooper Nuclear Station at Brownville is the state's operating nuclear plant. Fort Calhoun Station north of Omaha is being decommissioned. Boilers, piping, turbines and condensers need UT, MT, PT and ET during outages. Nuclear in-service inspection follows ASME Section XI and has its own additional qualification requirements on top of SNT-TC-1A.
  • Rail. Union Pacific is headquartered in Omaha, and rail shops and contractors across the region inspect wheels, axles, bogies, bridges and rail. UT and MT dominate, under railroad and AAR requirements.
  • Ethanol, food and agricultural processing. Ethanol plants, grain processors and meat and food plants across Nebraska and western Iowa operate tanks, pressure vessels and process piping that need UT thickness, PT and VT, typically under API 510, API 570 and API 653 inspection programmes.
  • Bridges and transportation. The Missouri River crossings and the Nebraska and Iowa DOT bridge inventories generate inspection and fabrication work for UT, MT and VT technicians.
  • Construction and engineering firms. Large engineering and construction companies headquartered in Omaha hire QA/QC and NDT staff for power, industrial and pipeline projects nationwide. Pipeline welding follows API 1104.
  • Military aviation. Offutt Air Force Base in Bellevue hosts aircraft maintenance. Air Force NDI technicians train through military schools and work to Air Force technical orders, and contractors supporting the base may work to NAS 410. Atlantis does not offer NAS 410 training. We mention it only so you know what aviation employers may ask for.

Radiation licensing in Nebraska (and TWIC)

Nebraska signed its NRC Agreement State agreement on 1 October 1966, one of the first states to do so. The Office of Radiological Health within the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services licenses and inspects users of radioactive material, including industrial radiography, under Title 180 of the Nebraska Administrative Code. Nuclear power plants and federal facilities remain under direct NRC jurisdiction. A radiography company working in Nebraska needs the right state licence or reciprocity, and its radiographers must meet the radiation-safety training and certification rules, usually including certification from a recognised independent radiographer certification programme. That is separate from your SNT-TC-1A RT certification, which covers technique and interpretation. Our RT courses teach the method and do not replace the state's radiation-safety requirements. Confirm current requirements with DHHS before mobilising.

TWIC is a smaller issue in Omaha than on the coasts, because there are few maritime-security-regulated facilities in the area. Technicians who travel to coastal refineries, ports or terminals for national contractors will need one, though. Nuclear plants and military bases have their own access screening, which can take weeks. Start these early.

Method spotlight: MT and UT on poles, towers and structural weldments

The method combination that defines much of Omaha's inspection work is MT and UT on welded steel structures, especially tubular poles, towers and high-mast structures. These parts are often hot-dip galvanised after welding, and the base-plate and pole-to-flange connections are fatigue-sensitive. Cracks can start at weld toes during fabrication or galvanising, or develop in service under wind loading. A good technician knows where to look, how to prepare the surface without destroying the coating, and how to use UT to check full-penetration welds that MT cannot see into. Our MT and UT Level II courses use structural weld examples and AWS D1.1 acceptance criteria, and they cover documentation that a structural engineer or owner can use. Before your exams, use UT Level 2 practice questions to check the basics.

Local options compared: NDT training around Omaha

Many people searching for NDT training in Omaha want a list of options. Here is an honest one, based on what we could confirm at the time of writing. Check details with each provider.

  • Southeast Community College, Milford. SCC's Nondestructive Testing Technology associate degree, taught at Milford west of Lincoln, is Nebraska's college NDT programme. It is a full-time, lab-heavy course covering VT, PT, MT, UT, RT and ET. It suits people who want a two-year degree before their first NDT job.
  • Metropolitan Community College, Omaha. MCC offers welding technology programmes, including pipe welding. These are not NDT programmes, but a welding background is a common route into weld inspection and NDT.
  • Iowa State University, Ames. ISU's Center for Nondestructive Evaluation offers an undergraduate minor and a graduate certificate in NDE for engineering students. It is an academic research route rather than a technician course.
  • Inspection companies and in-house programmes. Inspection service companies, utilities and large fabricators in the region train and certify their own technicians. Getting hired as a trainee is a common route.
  • ASNT local sections. ASNT's section directory lists no Nebraska-based section at the time of writing. The ASNT Iowa Section, based around Ames, is the nearest listed section and a good place to meet Level IIIs and employers.
  • Atlantis NDT. Live online theory with an ASNT Level III, onsite cohorts at your facility, written-practice support and Level III services for the employer. Atlantis suits employers who need crews trained to their own written practice without sending people away, and individuals whose employer will certify them. Atlantis does not run a physical school in Omaha and does not offer a degree.

Level III services and written practices for Omaha NDT companies

Many Omaha fabricators and contractors have skilled inspectors but a weak paper trail: no written practice, an outdated one, or one that does not cover the methods they now use. Customers, owners and auditors will ask for the written practice, qualified procedures, examination records, vision checks and OJT logs before they ask anything else.

Atlantis supports Omaha employers with:

  • Written-practice development, or a gap review of your current written practice against SNT-TC-1A and customer requirements.
  • Method procedures written to AWS D1.1, D1.5, ASME Section V or the code your customer specifies.
  • Examination preparation and administration under your written practice by an ASNT Level III.
  • Audit preparation so records are complete before a customer or owner arrives.
  • Outside Level III services for companies without one. See Level III consulting in Omaha.

For the full employer model see SNT-TC-1A training and certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Omaha company.

Practise before the practical exam

Production shops rarely have spare time on the equipment. The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The welding workshop scene matches a lot of Omaha fabrication work. See also Practical NDT in Omaha.

The simulator is for practice only. It does not replace the practical examination, which under SNT-TC-1A is performed on real specimens with real equipment and graded by a Level III.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He sets course content, reviews written practices and procedures, and oversees examinations under the employer's programme. For Level III candidates, see ASNT Level III training.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Omaha

How do I get NDT certified in Omaha?

Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. You complete formal training, build supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations under the employer's written practice, and pass a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and can support the examinations and written practice. Without an employer yet, you can either enrol in a college programme such as SCC's or take a Level I course and apply for trainee roles.

Can I take NDT training online in Nebraska?

Yes, for theory. Live online classes with a Level III can cover the classroom hours your written practice requires. The practical examination is done in person on real specimens. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

That depends on your written practice and on whether you already hold UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom hours and experience for each level, and employers can require more. Current figures are in our training-requirements matrix.

Do I need a licence for radiography in Nebraska?

The company needs a radioactive-material licence from the Nebraska DHHS Office of Radiological Health, or reciprocity, to perform industrial radiography with sealed sources. Radiographers must meet the state's radiation-safety training and certification rules, usually including certification from a recognised independent programme. That is separate from SNT-TC-1A RT certification. Work inside nuclear power plants falls under NRC rules.

What does NDT training cost in Omaha?

We quote on request because it depends on method, level, group size and whether training runs online, onsite or blended. Send those details and we return a quote within one business day. Get an Omaha quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Omaha employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard framework for fabrication, power, rail and construction NDT in Nebraska. Some employers also ask for AWS CWI for weld inspectors, API inspector certification for tank and piping inspectors, or NAS 410 for aviation work. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for NDT training with Atlantis?

GI Bill benefits apply only to programmes approved for VA education benefits, and WIOA training funds generally go only to providers on Nebraska's eligible training provider list. Atlantis does not claim either approval. If you need those funds, check the VA's WEAMS search and the state list, or look at approved college programmes. Employer-paid training is the most common route for SNT-TC-1A certification.

Can you train our crew at our Omaha shop or plant?

Yes. Onsite training at your facility is one of our main delivery modes, using your equipment and representative parts where the written practice allows, with practical examinations under Level III supervision.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Omaha?

No. Atlantis has no physical training centre in Omaha or any other city. Training runs live online or onsite at your facility.

Which NDT methods do Omaha employers ask for most?

VT, MT and UT for structural and production welds, UT thickness and PT for process plants, ET for power plant condensers and exchangers, and RT for pipeline and piping welds.

Do I need extra qualifications for nuclear plant NDT work?

Often, yes. Nuclear in-service inspection follows ASME Section XI, and some ultrasonic examinations need additional performance demonstration qualification on top of employer certification. Your employer will tell you what its programme requires.

What do NDT technicians earn in Omaha?

Pay varies with method, level, travel and overtime. For a sourced overview, see our NDT salary guide.
